# 0. Setup

```{r libraries-and-paths}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(arrow)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(readxl)

data_dir     <- here::here("data/klagenfurt")
ggn_data_dir <- here::here("data")
out_dir      <- file.path(data_dir, "correlations")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

klagenfurt <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "klagenfurt_master_full.rds"))
klag_border <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "klagenfurt_boundary.rds"))
cat("Columns:", ncol(klagenfurt), "| Rows:", nrow(klagenfurt), "\n")
```


# 1. Data Preparation

## 1.1 Join Accessibility Metrics

Walking time to the nearest Urban Atlas 2021 green space (classes 14110, 14130, 31000 and 40000, at least 500 m², as in Malta; class 32000, herbaceous vegetation, excluded), computed for this study (`mcda/klagenfurt_e2sfca_newpop.R`, since 2026-11-20): OpenStreetMap walking network (pedestrian filter in `mcda/walk_filter.R`), shortest paths at 5 km/h, network origin points every 50 m. A cell takes the mean time over the origin points inside it; cells without a point take the nearest point within 200 m plus the straight line walk to it, and cells with no point within 200 m have no value. An origin point inside a green patch has time 0, and a cell assigned to such a point gets 0. ATGreen's walking time (OSRM routing, including class 32000) is kept as a sensitivity analysis (`nearest_green_min_atg`, `priority_atg_walk`).

```{r join-accessibility}
access <- read_csv(
  here::here("data/klagenfurt/accessibility_klagenfurt/own_routing/e2sfca_own_routing_cells.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  transmute(unit_id = as.character(gid), nearest_green_min = own_nearest_min)
access_atg <- read_parquet(
  here::here("output/accessibility/outputs-accesibility/klagenfurt/new/klagenfurt_nearest_ua2021/results/final_metrics.parquet")
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(unit_id = as.character(unit_id), nearest_green_min_atg = nearest_green_sec / 60)

klagenfurt$ID <- as.character(klagenfurt$ID)

klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  left_join(access, by = c("ID" = "unit_id"), suffix = c("_old", "")) %>%
  left_join(access_atg, by = c("ID" = "unit_id"))
cat("Spearman, own routing vs ATGreen walking time:",
    round(cor(klagenfurt$nearest_green_min, klagenfurt$nearest_green_min_atg, method = "spearman",
              use = "complete.obs"), 3), "\n")

cat("Accessibility matched:", sum(!is.na(klagenfurt$nearest_green_min)),
    "out of", nrow(klagenfurt), "\n")
summary(klagenfurt$nearest_green_min)
```

### Walking time histogram with category thresholds

I use a categorical normalization for walking time: 0–5 min (low priority), 5–10 min,
10–15 min, and >15 min (highest priority). 
```{r accessibility-histogram}
ggplot(klagenfurt %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% filter(!is.na(nearest_green_min)),
       aes(x = nearest_green_min)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#5DCAA5", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(5, 10, 15), linetype = "dashed", color = "#D85A30") +
  labs(title = "Walking time to nearest green space: Klagenfurt",
       subtitle = "Dashed lines = category thresholds (5, 10, 15 min)",
       x = "Minutes", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
```


## 1.2 Join Air Pollution (2021)

I have air pollution data for both 2018 and 2021, but 2021 has incomplete spatial coverage (It does not include the gridcell without population). So I compare the two years:
if the spatial pattern is stable and only the absolute level shifted,
I can fill missing 2021 cells using the 2018 values adjusted by the mean difference.

```{r join-air-pollution}
no2_21  <- read_csv(file.path(ggn_data_dir, "grid_no2_21.csv"))
pm25_21 <- read_csv(file.path(ggn_data_dir, "grid_pm25_21.csv"))

no2_21$ID  <- as.character(no2_21$ID)
pm25_21$ID <- as.character(pm25_21$ID)

klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  left_join(no2_21  %>% select(ID, no2_avg_21),  by = "ID") %>%
  left_join(pm25_21 %>% select(ID, pm25_avg_21), by = "ID")

cat("NO2 2021 matched:",  sum(!is.na(klagenfurt$no2_avg_21)),  "out of", nrow(klagenfurt), "\n")
cat("PM2.5 2021 matched:", sum(!is.na(klagenfurt$pm25_avg_21)), "out of", nrow(klagenfurt), "\n")
```

### Coverage comparison: 2018 vs 2021

```{r coverage-comparison, fig.height=8}

  labs(title = "NO2 2018") + theme_void()

p2 <- ggplot(klagenfurt) +

  labs(title = "PM2.5 2018") + theme_void()

p3 <- ggplot(klagenfurt) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = no2_avg_21), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", na.value = "#D85A30", name = "NO2\nµg/m³") +
  labs(title = "NO2 2021 (gaps in orange)") + theme_void()

p4 <- ggplot(klagenfurt) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pm25_avg_21), color = NA) +

  labs(title = "PM2.5 2021 (gaps in orange)") + theme_void()

(p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4)
```

### Temporal stability check

```{r temporal-comparison}
both <- klagenfurt %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(no2_avg_18) & !is.na(no2_avg_21))

cat("Cells with both years:", nrow(both), "\n\n")
cat("NO2  — 2018 mean:", round(mean(both$no2_avg_18), 2),
    "| 2021 mean:", round(mean(both$no2_avg_21), 2),
    "| r =", round(cor(both$no2_avg_18, both$no2_avg_21), 3),
    "| Δ =", round(mean(both$no2_avg_21 - both$no2_avg_18), 2), "\n")
cat("PM2.5 — 2018 mean:", round(mean(both$pm25_avg_18), 2),
    "| 2021 mean:", round(mean(both$pm25_avg_21), 2),
    "| r =", round(cor(both$pm25_avg_18, both$pm25_avg_21), 3),
    "| Δ =", round(mean(both$pm25_avg_21 - both$pm25_avg_18), 2), "\n")
```

```{r scatterplots-2018-vs-2021}
p1 <- ggplot(both, aes(x = no2_avg_18, y = no2_avg_21)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "#D85A30", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "NO2: 2018 vs 2021", x = "2018", y = "2021") +

p2 <- ggplot(both, aes(x = pm25_avg_18, y = pm25_avg_21)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "#D85A30", linetype = "dashed") +

  theme_minimal()

p1 + p2
```

### Gap-filling decision
The spatial pattern didn't change much between 2018 and 2021 (high correlations), only the
absolute levels shifted. I use `coalesce()` to fill missing 2021 cells with the 2018 value
adjusted by the mean difference between years. This creates a "final" variable for each
pollutant that has complete spatial coverage.- to check-

```{r gap-filling}
klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  mutate(
    no2_final  = coalesce(no2_avg_21, no2_avg_18 - 3.35),
    pm25_final = coalesce(pm25_avg_21, pm25_avg_18 - 0.97)
  )

cat("NO2 still missing:",  sum(is.na(klagenfurt$no2_final)), "\n")
cat("PM2.5 still missing:", sum(is.na(klagenfurt$pm25_final)), "\n")
```

```{r final-pollution-maps}
p1 <- ggplot(klagenfurt) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = no2_final), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", na.value = "#D85A30", name = "NO2\nµg/m³") +
  labs(title = "NO2 final (gap-filled)") + theme_void()

p2 <- ggplot(klagenfurt) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pm25_final), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", na.value = "#D85A30", name = "PM2.5\nµg/m³") +
  labs(title = "PM2.5 final (gap-filled)") + theme_void()

p1 + p2
```


## 1.3 Fill Traffic NAs
Traffic volume data only exists for cells on major roads. Cells without major roads are
not "missing" — they genuinely have no major-road traffic. I fill them with 0, but I will try to find the way they reflect low traffic, and not necessary 0.

```{r fill-traffic}
cat("Traffic NAs before:", sum(is.na(klagenfurt$new_trafficvol)), "\n")
klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  mutate(new_trafficvol = replace_na(new_trafficvol, 0))
cat("Traffic NAs after:", sum(is.na(klagenfurt$new_trafficvol)), "\n")
```

## 1.4 Variable Definitions

All six MCDA input variables. Direction = "benefit" means higher values → worse conditions → higher priority for greening intervention.

"Vulnerable population" is the 6th criterion from the survey but I don't have
the spatial data for it yet. It will be added later (composite index from elderly people and SES)

```{r variable-info}
var_info <- tibble::tribble(
  ~var,                ~label,                     ~unit,   ~direction,
  "lst",               "Land Surface Temperature", "°C",    "benefit",
  "dist_bs",           "Distance to Blue Space",   "m",     "benefit",
  "new_trafficvol",    "Traffic Volume",            "count", "benefit",
  "no2_final",         "NO2 (annual mean)",         "µg/m³", "benefit",
  "pm25_final",        "PM2.5 (annual mean)",       "µg/m³", "benefit",
  "nearest_green_min", "Time to Green Space",       "min",   "benefit"
)
```


# 2. Descriptive Statistics

```{r descriptive-stats}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 14, fig.height = 6
)
mcda_vars <- var_info$var

desc_stats <- klagenfurt %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(all_of(mcda_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n_valid   = sum(!is.na(value)),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(value)),
    min       = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    p2        = quantile(value, 0.02, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1        = quantile(value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median    = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean      = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3        = quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    p98       = quantile(value, 0.98, na.rm = TRUE),
    max       = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd        = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    skewness  = (mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) - median(value, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(var_info, by = c("variable" = "var")) %>%
  relocate(label, unit, .after = variable)

desc_stats %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Descriptive statistics of MCDA input variables") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## 3.2 Traffic Volume 
Only ~10% of cells have any traffic data (major roads only), so the distribution is extremely zero-inflated. Among non-zero cells, the
log-scale density reveals a bimodal shape — a small cluster of low-traffic cells and a large peak around 500–1000 vehicles.

I explored two normalization approaches:

1. **Categorical** (main): collapse into 3 levels based on natural breaks
2. **Log capped at p98** (sensitivity): continuous but handles zeros and outliers

```{r traffic-overview, fig.height=4}
#I am keeping just major roads, that means, take out all the gridcells where traffic=0. The big green bar at the left isn't zeros, it's the very small non-zero values (like 1–20).
traffic_valid <- klagenfurt %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(new_trafficvol > 0)

cat("Cells with traffic data:", nrow(traffic_valid),
    "out of", nrow(klagenfurt),
    paste0("(", round(100 * nrow(traffic_valid) / nrow(klagenfurt), 1), "%)"), "\n")

p1 <- ggplot(traffic_valid, aes(x = new_trafficvol)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#5DCAA5", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Raw distribution (non-zero only)", x = "Traffic volume", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(traffic_valid, aes(x = new_trafficvol)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#85B7EB", color = "white") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Log scale (non-zero only)", x = "Traffic volume (log)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

p1 + p2
```

# 4. Correlation Analysis

Spearman rank correlation between the raw MCDA variables. I use Spearman because most
variables don't follow a normal distribution. The goal is to check for redundancy:
if two variables have |r| > 0.70, they may be measuring the same spatial dimension
and I need to decide how to handle that.

**Key findings:**

- NO2 and PM2.5 have r = 0.77, which is above the 0.70 threshold. Since both represent
  "air pollution", I treat them as sub-indicators of a single criterion and split the
  citizen-derived air pollution weight equally between them.
- LST correlates moderately with time to green (0.67) and NO2 (0.64). These are expected
  (heat islands lack vegetation and have traffic) but the variables capture different
  dimensions (thermal stress vs. accessibility vs. air quality), so I keep all three.
- Distance to blue space is essentially independent of everything else (~0). Good — it
  adds unique spatial information.
- Traffic is weakly correlated with other variables (max r = 0.36 with NO2). Expected
  since only 10% of cells have traffic data.

```{r correlation-function}
cor_labs <- c(lst               = "LST",
              dist_bs           = "Dist. Blue Space",
              new_trafficvol    = "Traffic",
              no2_final         = "NO2",
              nearest_green_min = "Time to Green",
              pm25_final        = "PM2.5")

run_cor <- function(df, vars, title) {
  df_cor <- df %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% select(all_of(vars)) %>% drop_na()
  cat("Complete cases for correlation:", nrow(df_cor), "\n")
  mat <- cor(df_cor, method = "spearman")
  rownames(mat) <- cor_labs[rownames(mat)]
  colnames(mat) <- cor_labs[colnames(mat)]
  ggcorrplot(mat, type = "lower", lab = TRUE, lab_size = 3.5,
             colors = c("#D85A30", "white", "#1D9E75"),
             title = title,
             ggtheme = theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
}
```

```{r correlation-plot}
mcda_vars_cor <- c("lst", "dist_bs", "new_trafficvol", "no2_final",
                   "nearest_green_min", "pm25_final")

run_cor(klagenfurt, mcda_vars_cor, "Spearman correlation – Klagenfurt MCDA inputs")
```

Makes sense. There is a strong correlation between NO2 and PM2.5, which are both indicators of air pollution. Still I think it worth using a composite indicator (dividing the weight for air pollution equally between both variables) 
# 5. Normalization
All variables are normalized to [0, 1] where **1 = highest priority for greening**.
Normalization strategy per variable (decided after examining the distributions above):
| Variable | Method | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| LST | min-max, capped at p98 | Near-normal distribution. No absolute health threshold for satellite-derived LST, so treated as relative intra-urban variation. |
| Dist. blue space | min-max, capped at p98 | Skewness = 0.11 (essentially symmetric), so log is unnecessary — tested and confirmed it distorts the distribution. |
| NO2 | log + min-max, capped at p98 | Right-skewed, log compresses the tail and spreads the bulk. |
| PM2.5 | min-max, capped at p98 | Narrow range (7.5–16 µg/m³), near-normal. |
| Time to green | Categorical (0–5, 5–10, 10–15, >15 min) | Extremely right-skewed (most cells < 5 min). The health-relevant distinction is between "easily walkable" and "not". |
<!-- TODO: update text (2026-11-19): walking time to green is now continuous, min-max capped at p98 (spec 3.4), as in Malta. -->
<!-- TODO: update text: the traffic row says <=50 = 0, the code cuts at 7. -->
<!-- TODO: update text (2026-11-24): traffic is now OSM road type K3 (spec 3.4); the OpenTransportMap classes in the row below are norm_traffic_cat_otm, sensitivity only. -->

| Traffic | Categorical (≤50 = 0, 50–564 = 0.5, >564 = 1) | 90% zero-inflated. Only 10% of cells have major road data. Bimodal among non-zero cells. |

Traffic sensitivity analysis: log of values capped at p98 (continuous alternative).

## Cells not eligible for greening (water)

Added 2026-11-25 (spec 1.3): cells whose majority Urban Atlas class is water (50000) are not eligible
for greening and are not scored, with the same majority rule as the Malta airport and port constraint
(shared function `mcda/ua_constraint.R`). Klagenfurt uses Urban Atlas 2018 because the 2021 layer was
not available on 25 November 2026 (to be checked against 2021 when it can be downloaded). Constraint
cells are excluded from every normalisation bound.

```{r eligibility-mask}
source(here::here("mcda/ua_constraint.R"))
ua18 <- read_csv(here::here("data/klagenfurt/klagenfurt_ua2018_class_area_cells.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(ID = col_character(), .default = col_double()))
ua_major_k <- ua_pieces_from_table(ua18, "ID") %>% ua_majority() %>%
  transmute(ID = id, ua_code_2018 = ua_code, water_share_ua = water_share)
klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  select(-any_of(c("ua_code_2018", "ua_not_eligible", "water_share_ua", "water_cell"))) %>%
  mutate(ID_chr = as.character(ID)) %>%
  left_join(ua_major_k, by = c("ID_chr" = "ID")) %>%
  select(-ID_chr) %>%
  mutate(ua_not_eligible = ua_constrained(ua_code_2018, "Klagenfurt"),
         water_cell      = ua_not_eligible)
stopifnot(nrow(klagenfurt) == 12418, n_distinct(klagenfurt$ID) == 12418, sum(!is.na(klagenfurt$ua_code_2018)) == 11996)

table(klagenfurt$ua_code_2018[klagenfurt$ua_not_eligible], useNA = "ifany")
cat("Constraint (water) cells:", sum(klagenfurt$ua_not_eligible),
    "| water share > 50% (information only):", sum(klagenfurt$water_share_ua > 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    "| cells without Urban Atlas 2018 data:", sum(is.na(klagenfurt$ua_code_2018)), "\n")
summary(klagenfurt$water_share_ua)
hist(klagenfurt$water_share_ua[klagenfurt$water_share_ua > 0], breaks = 40, main = "Water share of the cell (cells with any water)", xlab = "")
ggplot(klagenfurt) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = ifelse(ua_not_eligible, "Water", "Eligible")), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Eligible = "grey85", Water = "#2c7fb8"), name = "Constraint") +
  theme_void()
```

```{r normalization}
normalize_minmax <- function(x, lower = NULL, upper = NULL) {
  if (is.null(lower)) lower <- min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(upper)) upper <- max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  x <- pmin(x, upper)
  x <- pmax(x, lower)
  (x - lower) / (upper - lower)
}

# Bounds over eligible cells only (water cells excluded from every bound, 2026-11-25)
elig_k <- !klagenfurt$ua_not_eligible
p98_traffic <- quantile(klagenfurt$new_trafficvol[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)

# Traffic (spec 3.4, decided 2026-11-24): OSM road type in three classes (K3), tunnels excluded, built by
# mcda/traffic_road_type_k3.R (same function in both cities). K2 and K5 kept for the sensitivity analysis.
# The previous OpenTransportMap classes (new_trafficvol) are kept as norm_traffic_cat_otm.
source(here::here("mcda/traffic_road_type_k3.R"))
rt_klag <- road_type_k3(
  klagenfurt, "ID",
  osm_path  = here::here("data/klagenfurt/accessibility_klagenfurt/own_routing/osm_highways_raw.gpkg"),
  tags_path = here::here("data/klagenfurt/accessibility_klagenfurt/own_routing/osm_tunnel_covered_tags_2026-11-24.json"),
  boundary  = klag_border)
stopifnot(identical(as.character(rt_klag$cells$ID), as.character(klagenfurt$ID)))
klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  mutate(road_class = rt_klag$cells$road_class, traffic_k2 = rt_klag$cells$K2,
         traffic_k3 = rt_klag$cells$K3, traffic_k5 = rt_klag$cells$K5)
# Sensitivity: CAMS-REG vehicle km per cell (mcda/traffic_cams_reg_check.Rmd, Step 3, without service and track;
# copied from output/figures_mcda/traffic_cams_reg_check/ to data/ on 2026-11-25, md5 identical)
cams_vkm_k <- read_csv(here::here("data/klagenfurt/traffic_vkm_klagenfurt_cams.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(cams_vkm_k) == 12418)
klagenfurt$traffic_vkm_cams <- cams_vkm_k$traffic_vkm[match(as.character(klagenfurt$ID), as.character(cams_vkm_k$ID))]
stopifnot(!anyNA(klagenfurt$traffic_vkm_cams))

klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  mutate(
    # ── Heat ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    norm_lst = normalize_minmax(lst,
                                lower = min(lst[elig_k], na.rm = TRUE),
                                upper = quantile(lst[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)),

    # ── Distance to blue space ────────────────────────────────
    norm_dist_bs = normalize_minmax(dist_bs,
                                    lower = 0,
                                    upper = quantile(dist_bs[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)),

    # ── NO2 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    norm_no2 = normalize_minmax(log1p(no2_final),
                                lower = log1p(min(no2_final[elig_k], na.rm = TRUE)),
                                upper = log1p(quantile(no2_final[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE))),

    # ── PM2.5 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    norm_pm25 = normalize_minmax(pm25_final,
                                 lower = min(pm25_final[elig_k], na.rm = TRUE),
                                 upper = quantile(pm25_final[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)),

    # ── Accessibility: time to green space ────────────────────
    # Continuous, min-max capped at p98, as in Malta (spec 3.4, decided 2026-11-19); before, 4
    # classes (0-5, 5-10, 10-15, >15 min). Missing walking time stays missing (available weight rule)
    # p98 over eligible cells (water cells excluded since 2026-11-25, spec 1.3)
    norm_green_time = normalize_minmax(nearest_green_min,
                                       lower = 0,
                                       upper = quantile(nearest_green_min[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Sensitivity: ATGreen's walking time (OSRM, including class 32000), same normalisation
    norm_green_time_atg = normalize_minmax(nearest_green_min_atg,
                                           lower = 0,
                                           upper = quantile(nearest_green_min_atg[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)),

    # Traffic (spec 3.4, since 2026-11-24): OSM road type, K3 (main 1, distributor 0.5, local or none 0)
    norm_traffic_cat = traffic_k3,
    # Sensitivity variants (spec 5.3): K2, K5, CAMS-REG vehicle km (log10(x + 1), min max 0 to p98, capped;
    # eligible cells), and the previous OpenTransportMap classes (main until 2026-11-23)
    norm_traffic_k2 = traffic_k2,
    norm_traffic_k5 = traffic_k5,
    norm_traffic_cams = normalize_minmax(log10(traffic_vkm_cams + 1), lower = 0,
                                         upper = quantile(log10(traffic_vkm_cams + 1)[elig_k], 0.98)),
    # ── Traffic: previous main (OpenTransportMap categorical), sensitivity only ──
    norm_traffic_cat_otm = case_when(
      new_trafficvol <= 7    ~ 0.0,
      new_trafficvol <= 564  ~ 0.5,
      TRUE                   ~ 1.0
    ),

    # ── Traffic: SENSITIVITY (log capped at p98) ──────────────
    norm_traffic_log = normalize_minmax(log1p(pmin(new_trafficvol, p98_traffic)),
                                        lower = 0,
                                        upper = log1p(p98_traffic)),

    # ── SES: Income (main) ────────────────────────────────────
    # Inverted: low income = high priority. Capped at p2–p98.
    norm_income_weighted = 1 - normalize_minmax(
      income_weighted,
      lower = quantile(income_weighted[elig_k], 0.02, na.rm = TRUE),
      upper = quantile(income_weighted[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),

    # ── SES: Income raw (sensitivity) ─────────────────────────
    norm_income = 1 - normalize_minmax(
      income,
      lower = quantile(income[elig_k], 0.02, na.rm = TRUE),
      upper = quantile(income[elig_k], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )

# Sanity checks for the traffic criterion (spec 3.4, K3 since 2026-11-24)
cat("Road type tunnels dropped (km by class):\n")
print(st_drop_geometry(rt_klag$tunnels) %>% group_by(class) %>% summarise(km = round(sum(km), 2), ways = n()))
cat("Cells whose class changes with the tunnel rule:", sum(rt_klag$cells$K3 != rt_klag$cells$K3_with_tunnels), "\n")
print(table(road_class = klagenfurt$road_class, norm_traffic_cat = klagenfurt$norm_traffic_cat))
summary(klagenfurt$norm_traffic_cat)
summary(klagenfurt$norm_traffic_cams)
ggplot(klagenfurt) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = factor(norm_traffic_cat, levels = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("Local or none", "Distributor", "Main"))),
          colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey90", "#9e9ac8", "#54278f"), name = "Traffic (K3)") +
  theme_void()

# Main analysis variable set
norm_vars <- c("norm_lst", "norm_dist_bs", "norm_no2", "norm_pm25",
               "norm_green_time", "norm_traffic_cat", "norm_income_weighted")

# Sensitivity: swap norm_traffic_cat → norm_traffic_log
# norm_vars_sens <- c("norm_lst", "norm_dist_bs", "norm_no2", "norm_pm25",
#                     "norm_green_time", "norm_traffic_log", "norm_income")
```


## 5.1 Normalization Summary

```{r normalization-summary}
norm_all <- c(norm_vars, "norm_traffic_log", "norm_income")

klagenfurt %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(all_of(norm_all)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n_valid   = sum(!is.na(value)),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(value)),
    min       = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    p2        = quantile(value, 0.02, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1        = quantile(value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median    = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean      = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3        = quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    p98       = quantile(value, 0.98, na.rm = TRUE),
    max       = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd        = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3))) %>%
  arrange(variable) %>%
  kable(caption = "Summary of normalized variables") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# 6. Citizen Survey Analysis

## 6.1 Sample Description

The survey used a budget allocation method: each respondent distributed a hypothetical
€1,000,000 across 6 criteria for prioritizing green space interventions in Klagenfurt.
The criteria were derived from stakeholder interviews and thematic analysis.

```{r load-survey}
source(here::here("R/read_survey.R"))  # 2026-11-06: surveys are .xlsx now
survey <- read_survey(here::here("data/klagenfurt/klagenfurtsurvey_nov26.xlsx"), dot_names = TRUE)
# 2 neighbourhood answers in the export are Latin-1, the rest UTF-8; re-encode the invalid ones
# (2026-11-05; without this, plotting fails with "invalid string in PangoCairo_Text")
survey <- survey %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ ifelse(validUTF8(.), ., iconv(., "latin1", "UTF-8"))))

budget_cols <- c("alloc_1_TooHotStreets",
                 "alloc_2_GreenOutOfReach",
                 "alloc_3_LowIncomeNeighborhoods",
                 "alloc_4_HighTrafficAreas",
                 "alloc_5_PoorAirQuality",
                 "alloc_6_DisconnectedNatureWater")
```

### Residency status cleanup

The xlsx export auto-converted two of the `resident` text categories into spreadsheet
date serials ("1-5" -> day 1, month 5 -> 46143; "5-10" -> day 5, month 10 -> 46300),
so they're mapped back here. `"left-2-plus"` (respondents who used to live in
Klagenfurt but left) isn't a residency-duration category and is excluded from the
survey entirely.

```{r resident-cleanup}
resident_levels <- c("born", "0-1", "1-5", "5-10", "10+")
KEEP_FORMER_RESIDENTS <- FALSE  # 2026-11-17: back to excluding former residents (n = 184); TRUE was for the UT2026 poster only

n_before <- nrow(survey)

survey <- survey %>%
  mutate(resident = case_when(
    resident %in% c("46143", "46143.0") ~ "1-5",
    resident %in% c("46300", "46300.0") ~ "5-10",
    TRUE                                ~ resident
  )) %>%
  # UT2026 poster (2026-11-05): keep the 2 former residents so the weights stay those of the saved
  # map and Figure 4 (n = 186 with the 2026-11-06 export; 184 before). Set to FALSE to exclude them (n = 184).
  { if (KEEP_FORMER_RESIDENTS) . else filter(., resident != "left-2-plus") } %>%
  mutate(resident = factor(resident, levels = c(resident_levels, if (KEEP_FORMER_RESIDENTS) "left-2-plus")))

cat("Excluded 'left-2-plus':", n_before - nrow(survey), "respondents (KEEP_FORMER_RESIDENTS =",
    KEEP_FORMER_RESIDENTS, ")\n")
cat("Resident categories after cleanup:\n")
print(table(survey$resident, useNA = "ifany"))
```

### Neighbourhood name cleanup

`neighborhood` mixes proper German umlauts and ASCII transliterations for the same
place (`wölfnitz` vs. `woelfnitz`), and one entry has a typo (`waidmannsdort` for
`waidmannsdorf`). Canonicalized here to one display label per neighbourhood; `st_ruprecht_viktringer_vorstadt`/`welzenegg_voelkermarkter_vorstadt` are combined
statistical districts and are kept separate from the standalone
`viktringer_vorstadt`/`völkermarkter_vorstadt` answers since those are distinct
official Klagenfurt Stadtteile.

```{r neighborhood-cleanup}
neighborhood_labels <- c(
  "hallegg"                           = "Hallegg",
  "st_martin"                         = "St. Martin",
  "viktringer_vorstadt"               = "Viktringer Vorstadt",
  "völkermarkter_vorstadt"            = "Völkermarkter Vorstadt",
  "wölfnitz"                          = "Wölfnitz",
  "woelfnitz"                         = "Wölfnitz",
  "villacher_vorstadt"                = "Villacher Vorstadt",
  "hoertendorf"                       = "Hörtendorf",
  "st_peter_fischl"                   = "St. Peter-Fischl",
  "st_ruprecht_viktringer_vorstadt"   = "St. Ruprecht-Viktringer Vorstadt",
  "feschnig_st_veiter_vorstadt"       = "Feschnig-St. Veiter Vorstadt",
  "innere_stadt_ring"                 = "Innere Stadt-Ring",
  "kreuzbergl_villacher_vorstadt"     = "Kreuzbergl-Villacher Vorstadt",
  "annabichl"                         = "Annabichl",
  "viktring"                          = "Viktring",
  "welzenegg_voelkermarkter_vorstadt" = "Welzenegg-Völkermarkter Vorstadt",
  "st_martin_waidmannsdort"           = "St. Martin-Waidmannsdorf"
)

survey <- survey %>%
  mutate(neighborhood = recode(neighborhood, !!!neighborhood_labels))

cat("Neighbourhood categories after cleanup:\n")
print(sort(table(survey$neighborhood, useNA = "ifany")))
```

```{r sample-description}
cat("Total responses:", nrow(survey), "\n\n")

# Flag rows with NAs in budget columns before imputing
n_incomplete <- sum(!complete.cases(survey[budget_cols]))
cat("Rows with NA in budget cols:", n_incomplete, "\n")

# Replace NA budget values with 0: respondents who left a criterion blank
# allocated their full budget to the remaining criteria (row sums to €1,000,000
# with na.rm = TRUE), so NA is treated as €0 for that criterion.
survey <- survey %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(budget_cols), ~replace_na(., 0)))

survey_sums <- survey %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(total = sum(c_across(all_of(budget_cols)))) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("All budgets sum to €1,000,000:", all(survey_sums$total == 1000000), "\n")
cat("Budget totals:\n")
print(table(survey_sums$total))

survey_clean <- survey
cat("\nUsing", nrow(survey_clean), "responses for analysis\n")
```

## 6.3 Green space behaviour

```{r green-space-behaviour, fig.height=14}
freq_labels <- c("0" = "Never", "1" = "Once/week", "2-4" = "2–4×/week", "5-7" = "Daily")

p_freq <- survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(visitFrequency)) %>%
  mutate(freq = factor(visitFrequency, levels = names(freq_labels), labels = freq_labels)) %>%
  count(freq) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = freq, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#5DCAA5") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, "\n(", pct, "%)")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  labs(title = "How often do you visit green spaces?", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  ylim(0, max(table(survey$visitFrequency)) * 1.25) +
  theme_minimal()

p_nearby <- survey %>%
  count(greenNearby) %>%
  filter(!is.na(greenNearby)) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = greenNearby, y = n, fill = greenNearby)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, "\n(", pct, "%)")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("yes" = "#5DCAA5", "no" = "#D85A30")) +
  labs(title = "Green space within walking distance?", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

reasons_df <- survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(visitReasons)) %>%
  mutate(
    Relaxation = str_detect(visitReasons, "relax"),
    Social     = str_detect(visitReasons, "friends"),
    Sport      = str_detect(visitReasons, "sport")
  )

p_reasons <- reasons_df %>%
  summarise(Relaxation = sum(Relaxation),
            Social     = sum(Social),
            Sport      = sum(Sport)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "reason", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / nrow(reasons_df), 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(reason, n), y = n, fill = reason)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", pct, "%)")), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Relaxation = "#5DCAA5", Social = "#85B7EB", Sport = "#F0997B")) +
  coord_flip() +
  ylim(0, nrow(reasons_df) * 1.15) +
  labs(title = "Why do you visit green spaces?",
       subtitle = paste0("Multiple answers allowed; n = ", nrow(reasons_df), " with response"),
       x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

p_combos <- survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(visitReasons)) %>%
  count(visitReasons, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
         lab = str_replace_all(visitReasons, ", ", " + ")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(lab, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#AFA9EC") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", pct, "%)")), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  ylim(0, max(table(survey$visitReasons)) * 1.25) +
  labs(title = "Reason combinations", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

p_neigh <- survey %>%
  count(neighborhood, sort = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(neighborhood)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(neighborhood, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#AFA9EC") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Neighbourhood of residence", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

(p_freq + p_nearby) / (p_reasons + p_combos) / p_neigh +
  plot_annotation(title = paste0("Green space behaviour and context — Klagenfurt (n = ", nrow(survey), ")"))
```

```{r green-space-behaviour-summary}
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover","condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  print()
```

## 6.4 Are Citizen Weights Significantly Different from Equal?

I test whether the mean allocation for each criterion is significantly different from
€166,667 (equal distribution = 1,000,000 / 6 criteria). This tells me whether citizens
actually differentiated between criteria or just spread the budget evenly.

```{r weight-significance}
equal_alloc <- 1000000 / length(budget_cols)

sig_results <- map_dfr(budget_cols, function(col) {
  vals <- survey_clean[[col]]
  test <- t.test(vals, mu = equal_alloc)
  tibble(
    criterion = col,
    mean      = mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    ci_lower  = test$conf.int[1],
    ci_upper  = test$conf.int[2],
    p_value   = test$p.value,
    sig       = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "")
  )
}) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean))

sig_results %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) %>%
  kable(caption = paste0("One-sample t-test: mean allocation vs €",
                         format(round(equal_alloc), big.mark = ","),
                         " (equal weights)")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r weight-significance-plot, fig.height=6}
sig_results %>%
  mutate(criterion = gsub("alloc_[0-9]_", "", criterion) %>%
           str_replace_all("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(criterion, mean), y = mean)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = equal_alloc, linetype = "dashed", color = "#D85A30") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Mean budget allocation with 95% confidence intervals",
       subtitle = paste0("Dashed line = equal weight (€",
                         format(round(equal_alloc), big.mark = ","), ")"),
       x = NULL, y = "Mean allocation (€)") +
  theme_minimal()
```


# 7. Weighted Linear Combination

## 7.1 Weights

I use the citizen-derived weights from the survey. The mapping from survey criteria
to spatial variables is:

| Survey criterion | Spatial variable(s) |
|------------------|---------------------|
| 1. Too Hot Streets | norm_lst |
| 2. Green Out of Reach | norm_green_time |
| 3. Low Income Neighborhoods | **excluded** (no spatial data yet) |
| 4. High Traffic Areas | norm_traffic_cat |
| 5. Poor Air Quality | norm_no2 + norm_pm25 (weight split equally) |
| 6. Disconnected from Nature/Water | norm_dist_bs |

Air pollution (criterion 5) is represented by two sub-indicators: NO2 and PM2.5. Since their Spearman correlation is r = 0.77, I considered either a composite index
or splitting the weight. Mathematically, splitting the weight equally (w_no2 = w_pm25 = w_airpol / 2) is identical to computing a composite and applying
the full weight. I split to keep the variables explicit.

Criterion 3 (vulnerable population / low income neighborhoods) is excluded from the priority map because the spatial indicator is still in development. The remaining
weights are rescaled to sum to 1.

```{r define-weights}
raw_survey <- budget_summary %>%
  select(criterion, mean_alloc) %>%
  deframe()

raw_weights <- c(
  norm_lst          = raw_survey["alloc_1_TooHotStreets"],
  norm_green_time   = raw_survey["alloc_2_GreenOutOfReach"],
  norm_traffic_cat  = raw_survey["alloc_4_HighTrafficAreas"],
  norm_income_weighted = raw_survey["alloc_3_LowIncomeNeighborhoods"], 
  norm_no2          = raw_survey["alloc_5_PoorAirQuality"] / 2, #divided to two sub-indicators
  norm_pm25         = raw_survey["alloc_5_PoorAirQuality"] / 2, #same
  norm_dist_bs      = raw_survey["alloc_6_DisconnectedNatureWater"]
)
names(raw_weights) <- c("norm_lst", "norm_green_time", "norm_traffic_cat", "norm_income_weighted",
                         "norm_no2", "norm_pm25", "norm_dist_bs")

# Rescale to sum to 1 (criterion 3 excluded)
weights <- raw_weights / sum(raw_weights)

tibble(
  criterion    = names(weights),
  survey_avg   = round(raw_weights, 0),
  weight       = round(weights, 3),
  equal_weight = round(ifelse(names(weights) %in% c("norm_no2", "norm_pm25"), 1 / 12, 1 / 6), 3)
) %>%
  kable(caption = paste0("Citizen-derived weights vs equal weights (",
                         length(norm_vars),
                         " variables, vulnerable population excluded)")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```


## 7.2 Priority Scores

Available weight rule (adopted 2026-11-05 for the UT2026 poster; the HIA still uses the score saved
before this change, `klagenfurt_mcda_priority_may_pre_avail80.rds`). A cell is scored if its
available criteria carry at least 80% of the total citizen weight; the score is the weighted mean
over the available criteria, sum(w_i s_i) / sum(w_i). The equal weights score uses the same cells.

```{r compute-wlc}
MIN_WEIGHT_AVAILABLE <- 0.80
crit_mat <- function(df, w) as.matrix(as.data.frame(df)[, names(w), drop = FALSE])
klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  mutate(weight_available = as.numeric((!is.na(crit_mat(klagenfurt, weights))) %*% weights) / sum(weights),
         scored = weight_available >= MIN_WEIGHT_AVAILABLE - 1e-12 & !ua_not_eligible)

# Weighted mean over available criteria, NA for cells outside the scored set
wlc_avail <- function(df, w, keep = klagenfurt$scored) {
  S <- crit_mat(df, w)
  A <- !is.na(S)
  S[!A] <- 0
  den <- as.numeric(A %*% w)
  out <- as.numeric(S %*% w) / den
  out[!keep | den == 0] <- NA
  out
}
# Equal weights at the criterion level (spec 2.3): 6 criteria at 1/6, air quality split 1/12 NO2 + 1/12 PM2.5
# (fixed 2026-11-25; was 1/7 per indicator, air quality 2/7)
weights_equal <- setNames(rep(1 / 6, length(norm_vars)), norm_vars)
weights_equal[c("norm_no2", "norm_pm25")] <- 1 / 12
stopifnot(abs(sum(weights_equal) - 1) < 1e-12)

klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>%
  mutate(priority_equal   = wlc_avail(klagenfurt, weights_equal),
         priority_citizen = wlc_avail(klagenfurt, weights))

# Sanity checks: missing values, available weight, scored cells, score distribution
colSums(is.na(crit_mat(klagenfurt, weights)))
summary(klagenfurt$weight_available)
table(n_missing = rowSums(is.na(crit_mat(klagenfurt, weights))), scored = klagenfurt$scored)
summary(klagenfurt$priority_citizen)
hist(klagenfurt$priority_citizen, breaks = 60, main = "priority_citizen (available weight rule)", xlab = "")
```

# 8. Sensitivity Analysis

## 8.1 Robustness to weight perturbations

Each citizen weight is perturbed by ±20% in turn (remaining weights rescaled to sum to 1). Spearman r and top-quintile class agreement vs the baseline citizen-weighted priority surface.

```{r sensitivity-analysis}
perturbation <- 0.20

sensitivity_results <- map_dfr(names(weights), function(var) {
  map_dfr(c(-perturbation, perturbation), function(delta) {

    w_perturbed        <- weights
    w_perturbed[var]   <- weights[var] * (1 + delta)
    others             <- setdiff(names(weights), var)
    remaining          <- 1 - w_perturbed[var]
    w_perturbed[others] <- weights[others] / sum(weights[others]) * remaining

    perturbed_score <- wlc_avail(klagenfurt, w_perturbed)

    r <- cor(klagenfurt$priority_citizen, perturbed_score,
             use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman")

    q80_base <- quantile(klagenfurt$priority_citizen, 0.8, na.rm = TRUE)
    q80_pert <- quantile(perturbed_score,             0.8, na.rm = TRUE)
    top_base <- !is.na(klagenfurt$priority_citizen) & klagenfurt$priority_citizen >= q80_base
    top_pert <- !is.na(perturbed_score)             & perturbed_score             >= q80_pert
    overlap  <- sum(top_base & top_pert) / sum(top_base)

    tibble(
      variable      = var,
      direction     = ifelse(delta > 0, "+20%", "-20%"),
      spearman_r    = round(r, 4),
      top_q_overlap = round(overlap * 100, 1)
    )
  })
})

sensitivity_results %>%
  kable(
    caption   = "Sensitivity: effect of ±20% weight perturbation (Klagenfurt)",
    col.names = c("Variable", "Direction", "Spearman r", "Top-quintile overlap (%)")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

## Leave one out

Each criterion dropped in turn (air quality drops NO2 and PM2.5 together), the other citizen weights
rescaled to sum to 1, same cells and available weight rule (spec 5.3; added 2026-11-20).

```{r leave-one-out-k}
sens_cmp <- function(x, ref = klagenfurt$priority_citizen) {
  ok <- !is.na(ref) & !is.na(x)
  q_r <- dplyr::ntile(ref[ok], 5); q_x <- dplyr::ntile(x[ok], 5)
  tibble(spearman = cor(ref[ok], x[ok], method = "spearman"),
         top_quintile_retained_pct = 100 * mean(q_x[q_r == 5] == 5),
         cells_changing_quintile_pct = 100 * mean(q_x != q_r),
         cells = sum(ok))
}
crit_groups <- list(`Urban heat` = "norm_lst", `Blue space` = "norm_dist_bs",
                    `Air quality` = c("norm_no2", "norm_pm25"), `Green proximity` = "norm_green_time",
                    Traffic = "norm_traffic_cat", `Low income` = "norm_income_weighted")
stopifnot(setequal(unlist(crit_groups), names(weights)))
loo_k <- map_dfr(names(crit_groups), function(g) {
  w <- weights[!names(weights) %in% crit_groups[[g]]]
  sens_cmp(wlc_avail(klagenfurt, w / sum(w))) %>%
    mutate(criterion_dropped = g, citizen_weight_pct = 100 * sum(weights[crit_groups[[g]]]), .before = 1)
})
loo_k %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(., 3))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Leave one out: main score vs score without each criterion") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
summary(loo_k$spearman)
ggplot(loo_k, aes(reorder(criterion_dropped, spearman), spearman)) + geom_col(fill = "grey50") +
  coord_flip() + labs(x = NULL, y = "Spearman vs main score") + theme_minimal()
```

## Traffic variants (spec 5.3)

Added 2026-11-24 with the switch to road type K3. Each variant replaces `norm_traffic_cat`, citizen weights,
available weight rule; traffic has no missing values, so the scored cells do not change. Traffic excluded is
in the leave one out table.

```{r traffic-variants-k}
traffic_variants_k <- c(`Traffic: road type K2`                        = "norm_traffic_k2",
                        `Traffic: road type K5`                        = "norm_traffic_k5",
                        `Traffic: CAMS-REG vehicle km (log10(x + 1))`  = "norm_traffic_cams",
                        `Traffic: OpenTransportMap classes (previous)` = "norm_traffic_cat_otm")
traffic_scores_k <- map(traffic_variants_k, function(v) wlc_avail(klagenfurt %>% mutate(norm_traffic_cat = .data[[v]]), weights))
traffic_sens_k <- imap_dfr(traffic_scores_k, ~ sens_cmp(.x) %>% mutate(variant = .y, scored_cells = sum(!is.na(.x)), .before = 1))
traffic_sens_k %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(., 3))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Traffic variants vs the main score (cells scored in both)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
klagenfurt <- klagenfurt %>% mutate(priority_traffic_k2 = traffic_scores_k[[1]], priority_traffic_k5 = traffic_scores_k[[2]],
                                    priority_traffic_cams = traffic_scores_k[[3]], priority_traffic_otm = traffic_scores_k[[4]])
```

## Sensitivity summary for Table S6

All variants against the main score on the cells scored in both: Spearman, top quintile retained,
cells changing quintile (spec 5.1 and 5.2). Saved to `data/klagenfurt/klag_sensitivity.rds` for
`Tables_MCDA.Rmd`. The +/-20% rows are recomputed here with Spearman and top quintile retained.
`priority_equal` gives 1/6 per criterion (air quality 1/12 NO2 + 1/12 PM2.5), as in spec 2.3 (fixed
2026-11-25; before, 1/7 per indicator, air quality 2/7).

```{r sensitivity-summary-s6-k}
pert_k <- map_dfr(names(weights), function(v) map_dfr(c(-0.2, 0.2), function(delta) {
  w <- weights; w[v] <- weights[v] * (1 + delta)
  o <- setdiff(names(weights), v); w[o] <- weights[o] / sum(weights[o]) * (1 - w[v])
  sens_cmp(wlc_avail(klagenfurt, w))
}))
fmt_r <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x); fmt_p <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", x)
rng <- function(x, f) paste(f(min(x)), "to", f(max(x)))
row_of <- function(name, x) { r <- sens_cmp(x)
  tibble(test_name = name, spearman_r = fmt_r(r$spearman), class_agreement = fmt_p(r$top_quintile_retained_pct),
         cells_changing_quintile = fmt_p(r$cells_changing_quintile_pct)) }
klag_sensitivity <- bind_rows(
  row_of("Citizen vs equal weights", klagenfurt$priority_equal),
  tibble(test_name = "Each weight +/-20% (range)", spearman_r = rng(pert_k$spearman, fmt_r),
         class_agreement = rng(pert_k$top_quintile_retained_pct, fmt_p),
         cells_changing_quintile = rng(pert_k$cells_changing_quintile_pct, fmt_p)),
  loo_k %>% transmute(test_name = paste("Without", tolower(criterion_dropped)), spearman_r = fmt_r(spearman),
                      class_agreement = fmt_p(top_quintile_retained_pct),
                      cells_changing_quintile = fmt_p(cells_changing_quintile_pct)),
  imap_dfr(traffic_scores_k, ~ row_of(.y, .x)),
  row_of("Income: raw instead of spatially weighted", klagenfurt_inc$priority_income_raw),
  row_of("Walking time: ATGreen (OSRM)", klagenfurt$priority_atg_walk))
klag_sensitivity %>% kable(caption = "Sensitivity summary, Klagenfurt") %>% kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
saveRDS(klag_sensitivity, file.path(data_dir, "klag_sensitivity.rds"))
```
